o: Count length-5 palindromic subsequences of a digit string, modulo 1e9+7. Such a palindrome has the form a b c b a: a pair (a,b) before the middle c, and the mirrored pair (b,a) after it. In "103301" the middle can be the '3' at index 2 or 3 with (1,0) before and (0,1) after, giving two subsequences. With n up to 1e4 we fix the middle character and multiply (count of ab-pairs before) × (count of ba-pairs after), summed over all 100 digit pairs — O(100n).
k: Every length-5 palindrome is a·b·middle·b·a; fix the middle index and combine pair counts from both sides.
Precompute prefix single counts and suffix pair counts to evaluate each middle position in O(100).

a.i: Enumerate all C(n,5) index combinations and test each for being a palindrome. Only viable for tiny inputs; included to clarify the object being counted.
s: Check the selected digits read the same both ways.

a.n: Approach 2: Middle-position DP with pair counts
a.i: Sweep the middle index i from right to left. Maintain pre[a][b] = number of pairs (x<y<i) with digits a,b, and post[b][a] = number of pairs (i<y<z) with digits b,a. At each middle digit d, add Σ pre[a][b]·post[b][a]. Update post using the element at i+1 as a pair-start (paired with everything after it), and pre using element i as a pair-end (paired with everything before it). Prefix/suffix single-digit count arrays supply the update terms in O(10).
s: Precompute before[i][a] = count of digit a in s[0..i-1] and after[i][a] = count in s[i+1..n-1].
Sweep i from n-1 downto 0: first fold s[i+1] into post, then add Σ pre[a][b]·post[b][a] to the answer, then fold s[i] into pre.
a.sp: O(n) for the prefix/suffix count tables

w: The pair-decomposition around the middle is the whole problem; everything else is bookkeeping. Test carefully on "0000000" (expect 21 = C(7,5)) and "9999900000" (expect 2). Pitfalls: updating pre/post before vs. after reading the answer at each middle (order matters — pairs must lie strictly on one side), and taking products modulo 1e9+7 with 64-bit intermediates. Follow-up: generalize to length-7 palindromes by nesting one more pair layer.
